about: Every name the guide shows to a person comes from this list. Keep the term in English in every conversation language and explain it the first time it appears. `avoid` lists words that must not replace the term in plugin text.

trust.summary: Only a search summary of the source was read.
trust.practice: Widely used in the trade; no single source traced.
trust.unchecked: A named standard recalled from memory; not yet re-read for this list.
trust.coined: Named in this project or by its owner. Not an industry term.

inherited_from: Rows marked inherited carry the trust level recorded in the owner's architecture note of 2026-11-09; they were not re-read for this list.

terms.meaning: The smallest named design decisions: a colour, a spacing step, a type size.
terms.source: W3C Design Tokens Community Group, Technical Reports 2025.10

terms.meaning: Three layers of tokens: primitive (raw values), semantic (roles), component (bound to one component). The token format does not define them; teams choose.
The tier that holds design tokens and the rules for colour, typography, spacing, shape, elevation, motion, iconography and layout.
terms.source: Common practice (Material Design, Atlassian, Primer use it as a top-level section)

terms.meaning: One set of token values for one identity or mode. The structure of the tokens stays the same across themes.
The single colour a whole palette is derived from. Material Design 3 says source color; Flutter's API calls the same thing a seed colour.
terms.source: Material Design 3, How the system works (read 2026-11-11); Flutter, ColorScheme.fromSeed

terms.meaning: The tones of one key colour from black to white that color roles pick from. Tones run from 0 to 100.
terms.source: Material Design 3, How the system works (read 2026-11-11)

terms.meaning: What a colour is for (primary, on-primary, surface, outline), as opposed to which colour it is.
The luminance ratio between text or a control and what is behind it. At level AA: at least 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text, and 3:1 for interface components and graphical objects.
terms.source: WCAG 2.2, Understanding 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) and 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (read 2026-11-11)

terms.meaning: The smallest area a pointer control may offer: at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels at level AA, with exceptions.
The accessibility level a product commits to: A, AA or AAA. Levels add up: AA includes everything in A.
Whether people with disabilities can perceive and operate the product. Measured against a conformance level.
What the product is and who uses it, as far as it changes design decisions.
Whether people work in the screens (an application) or mostly read them (a content site).
The fixed set of type sizes, each a step from the one before.
A sequence of sizes related by one ratio, such as 1.25. The ratios are named after musical intervals: minor second, major second, minor third, major third, perfect fourth.
terms.source: Tim Brown, More Meaningful Typography, A List Apart, 2011; modularscale.com (read 2026-11-11)

terms.meaning: A family of letterforms, such as one sans-serif design in all its weights. CSS calls it a font family.
terms.source: Common practice in typography; CSS Fonts Module Level 4, font-family

terms.meaning: The typeface of running text: labels, cells, paragraphs, controls.
The typeface of headings. It may be the text typeface, or another one.

The sign a product is known by: a symbol, its name drawn as letters, or the two together, kept as files. Where a repository has none, the floor's mark is the product's name set in the heading typeface.
terms.source: Common practice in brand identity; the floor's mark is named in spec 0017

terms.meaning: What a file of the mark is for: the symbol alone (mark), the name drawn as letters (wordmark), the two side by side or one above the other (lockup), the icon a browser shows for a page (favicon), or the icon of an installed app (app icon).
terms.source: Common practice in brand guidelines; the roles of spec 0017

terms.meaning: How a file of the mark is coloured: in its colours, in one colour, or drawn for a dark ground (inverse).
The greys of a theme: its backgrounds, its text, its surfaces and their edges. Pure grey has no hue; a tinted grey leans a little to the source colour.
terms.source: Common practice in design systems that derive a theme from one colour

terms.meaning: The colours a product uses to say how something went: an error always, and success, a warning or information where the product needs them.
terms.source: Common practice; the standard decision status-tone

terms.meaning: The typeface each operating system uses for its own interface, named in CSS by the generic family system-ui. Nothing is loaded for it.
terms.source: Common practice; CSS names it with the generic family system-ui

terms.meaning: The distance between baselines of consecutive lines. Typographers call it leading.
The uniform space added between characters. Typographers call it tracking.
The length of a line of running text, counted in characters.
The fixed set of distances, usually multiples of one base unit.
The corner treatment of surfaces and controls, set as a corner radius scale.
terms.source: Common practice (Material Design names the section Shape)

terms.meaning: How round a corner is. Material Design 3 names a scale of them: none 0, extra small 4, small 8, medium 12, large 16, and larger steps up to full.
A fixed vertical step that line heights and spacing snap to, so text on different parts of a page lines up. Material Design 1 uses 4dp for type and 8dp for components.
How far a surface sits above another, shown by shadow or tone.
The durations and easing curves of transitions, and when a transition is allowed.
How tightly controls and rows are packed, as a named setting rather than per-component sizes.
Columns, gutters and margins that place content, with breakpoints where the arrangement changes.
The icon set and its drawing rules: grid, keylines, stroke weight.
A deliberate departure from the computed value because the eye reads the computed one as wrong. Recorded with its reason.
terms.source: Common practice in type and icon design

terms.meaning: Components from the smallest to larger groups. A description of size, not a folder layout.
Page-level objects that place components in a layout and state the structure of the content.
Templates filled with real content.
The components and conventions shared by the whole organisation.
terms.source: Brad Frost, The art of design system recipes

terms.meaning: The components of the core design system: the shared, closed set every product builds from.
terms.source: The owner's architecture note of 2026-11-09, after Brad Frost's core design system

terms.meaning: Compositions specific to one product. Outside the core, still built on its tokens.
terms.source: Brad Frost, The art of design system recipes

terms.meaning: One-off pieces used in a single place. They need a reason and an expiry.
terms.source: Brad Frost, The art of design system recipes

terms.meaning: A recipe that has proved its worth moves into the core.
terms.source: Brad Frost, The art of design system recipes

terms.meaning: The named parts of a component.
One of a closed set of looks or purposes a component offers.
What a component or a view shows because of a condition: hover, focus, pressed, disabled, selected for a control; loading, empty, error for a view.
A named place in a component that takes content.
Components that supply behaviour and accessibility with no styling.
How to build accessibility semantics into a widget such as a dialog, a combobox or tabs. The guide calls them patterns.
terms.source: W3C, ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG), Patterns (read 2026-11-11)

terms.meaning: Repeatable answers to a recurring task: saving, notifying, waiting, failing, being empty, searching, filtering.

A list of items and the one item opened from it, arranged together: side by side where both fit, one at a time where they do not. A side sheet over the list and a page of its own are the other arrangements.
terms.source: Common practice (Material Design 3 names list-detail among its canonical layouts)

terms.meaning: What a view shows when there is nothing yet, with the first action to take.
What a view shows while content is on its way, usually a skeleton of the coming content.
What a view shows when a request failed, with what failed and how to retry.
An action that removes something and cannot be undone. It asks for confirmation and names the thing.
The rules for words: voice and tone, button labels, error sentences, formats.
Voice is the constant character of the writing; tone is how it shifts with the situation.
Adapting a product to the language, cultural and other requirements of a target market (a locale). It covers numeric, date and time formats and the use of currency, among other things.

The kind of data a table column holds, which decides its alignment and formatting: numbers right-aligned, text left-aligned. No single industry name exists; Polaris says column content types, MUI column types, AG Grid cell data types.
terms.source: Shopify Polaris, Data table; MUI X Data Grid, Column definition; AG Grid, Cell data types (read 2026-11-11)

terms.meaning: The channel that delivers component code: a JSON index where each item lists its files and dependencies, installed into the project by a command.
The machine-readable index of components: options, variants, defaults.
A real build chosen as the model to copy.
The opinionated, supported way. Leaving it is allowed and unsupported.
terms.source: Spotify Engineering, How we use Golden Paths

terms.meaning: Shape the types so that a wrong state cannot be written.
Static checks that reject values and structures outside the system.
Whether what was built matches what the system decided, and the checks that show it.
terms.source: Common practice (the owner's architecture note of 2026-11-09 uses it as a cross-cutting layer)

terms.meaning: How the system reaches the repositories that use it: a registry for code, a plugin for checks and procedures.
terms.source: Common practice (the owner's architecture note of 2026-11-09 uses it as a cross-cutting layer)

terms.meaning: A review of what exists against what the system says, ending in a list of gaps.
Comparing rendered screens against approved images.
Who may change the system, how changes are reviewed, and how adoption is tracked. Includes the contribution model.
The share of the product built from the system's components, and the count of detached variants.
A short page that states one decision, its context and its consequences.
Shared test tools: test templates, readiness waits, break-it checks.
Five rungs for how firmly a decision is held, from cannot-be-written-wrong down to written guidance, plus design judgment.
Decisions with an automated check that can fail, divided by all decisions.

One of the moments in a repository's life at which the plugin acts: the repository is born, it meets the plugin, a feature needs a new block, every change, and periodically before handing over. Status gives one line for each.
terms.source: The owner's architecture document for the meta layer, section on the life of a repository, 2026-11-13

terms.meaning: The record, kept in the repository, of which version of the plugin its copy of the tool came from and the hash git gives that folder. What a lockfile is to a dependency.
terms.source: The specification of the command set, 2026-11-15

terms.meaning: Bringing the installed version of the plugin's tool into a repository that already runs a copy of it, after a preview of what would change. The Vietnamese of the documents says lên đời.
terms.source: Common practice: package managers upgrade a dependency to a newer version, and say what it changes before they do

terms.meaning: The document that says what a version changes for the one who takes it. Upgrade hands over the release notes of one repository: which tool files, ledger entries and decisions the installed version changes there.
terms.source: Common practice in software releases and in the change logs of design systems

terms.meaning: Every question that waits on the owner of a repository, gathered on one sheet, each with one recommendation and what it rests on, answered in one go. Decide prints it and writes the answers back with the name of the person who gave them and the date.
terms.source: The specification of the command set, 2026-11-15

terms.meaning: The questions that wait on the owner and are not rows of a design ledger, kept as data in the repository, one file per question, so that the decision sheet can list them and take their answers, and an agent can add one without touching a shared file. A repository may have none. It is not one of the ledgers of the contract.

The six parts every document of a command has, always in the same order: the cover, one page for the person who decides, the findings with their evidence, the recommendations with what each rests on, the next steps, and what the document does not see.
terms.source: The specification of the command set, 2026-11-15

terms.meaning: The document status hands over: where the design system of a repository stands, what waits on its owner, and what to run next, set on the document frame.
terms.source: The specification of the command set, 2026-11-15

terms.meaning: The document the audit hands over: what answers each standard decision and what holds the answer, the tier reached and what the next one lacks, set on the document frame.
terms.source: The specification of the command set, 2026-11-15

terms.meaning: The ledger of every block a repository took in: what it is and where its code is, where it came from and at which pin, which need it answers, and who approved it on which day. One need has one answer.
terms.source: The specification of the ledgers that stop riding pull requests, 2026-11-16; the trade speaks of an intake or a contribution process, not traced to one source

terms.meaning: A file a tool writes from a source, such as the component manifest from the components: a change goes to the source, and the file is written again from it rather than edited.
terms.source: Common practice in build tooling: generated or derived files

terms.meaning: Telling from a change which tests it can reach, so that only those run: here, which screens a change reaches through the files each screen imports, and the whole suite whenever that cannot be told.
terms.source: Common practice in testing and build tooling

terms.meaning: The check that every choice points at a row of the decision ledger and every judgment nobody confirmed waits on the decision sheet: a judgment a branch writes that no person answered and no question asks fails the gate, as does source that goes around a decided scale and a test that proves a decision with no row.
terms.source: The specification of the ledgers that stop riding pull requests, 2026-11-16

terms.meaning: A choice the machine never makes on the owner's behalf: here a new kind of screen and the brand colour. A branch that makes one fails the gate until the owner's answer keeps that very item.
terms.source: The specification of the ledgers that stop riding pull requests, 2026-11-16; the trade speaks of a design review or an approval gate

terms.meaning: Gathering every piece an interface is made of and setting the treatments of each kind side by side, so that duplicates and unintended inconsistencies show. The inventory command takes the store of a repository this way, from its ledgers and its code rather than from screenshots.
terms.source: Brad Frost, Interface Inventory, bradfrost.com, 10 July 2013 (read 2026-11-19)

terms.meaning: The ledger of the outside libraries a repository picks blocks from: for each, its pin, the order it is looked through in, where its catalog is kept, and how an item is taken in. One file per source.
terms.source: The specification of the reusable store, 2026-11-19

terms.meaning: A library made by someone else that a repository picks blocks from. It is not a store of the repository's: what is taken from it is copied in and recorded in the intake ledger.
terms.source: The specification of the reusable store, 2026-11-19, after the owner's architecture document for the meta layer

terms.meaning: The exact files or the exact version of a source a repository took, recorded so that any reader can tell whether it still has them. What a lockfile does for packages.

The list of what an external source offers, each item by name, kind, title and description, kept in the repository so that it can be searched without the network. It holds no code. It is not the component manifest, which lists the repository's own components.
Copying the code taken from a source into the repository, instead of depending on it, so that the build fetches nothing. Blocks taken in from a source are vendored.
terms.source: Go Modules Reference, Vendoring (read 2026-11-19, the section only as a summary)

terms.meaning: The three rungs a need goes down, and only when the rung above has nothing that fits: the repository's own store, then a pinned source, then made by hand.
terms.source: The owner's architecture document for the meta layer, section on the intake path, 2026-11-13

terms.meaning: The few pieces this plugin ships ready for a new repository on a floor it knows, such as the table with typed columns and the record panel.
Marking a thing of the store as on its way out, with why and what replaces it, while the screens that still use it keep working. The Vietnamese of the documents says cho nghỉ.
terms.source: Common practice in the change policies of design systems

terms.meaning: A thing taken from a source that no longer matches it: its pin differs from the source's current pin, or its file differs from what was taken in.

A short statement of what the design favours when two good options pull different ways, fixed by the owner before any value is chosen, so a recommendation can say which principle it rests on. The Vietnamese of the documents says nguyên tắc thiết kế.
terms.source: Common practice of design studios and design systems

terms.meaning: A whole proposal of how the product looks, its colour, type and shape chosen to go together and shown on the product's own screens, so a person picks a direction before tuning any single value. The Vietnamese of the documents says hướng đi.

The place this plugin keeps for one capability of a design system: the ledgers only it writes, what it hands out, the checks that hold it, and who decides there. A closed socket takes no plug from outside.
terms.source: The specification of capabilities, sockets and plugs, 2026-11-20

terms.meaning: What does the work at a socket: one of this plugin's own, or a tool from outside described by a plug file, chosen for a repository by its owner. The command that shows them and puts the choice to the owner is plugs.
terms.source: The specification of capabilities, sockets and plugs, 2026-11-20; the setup step of 2026-11-23

terms.meaning: The document the plugs command hands over: every socket of the capability table by stage, what it does, who works it, and each plug from outside with where it stands, its measure or an invitation to measure it, and what it needs and sends, set on the document frame.

A whole direction read from what a tool from outside made (a token file, a DESIGN.md, an export of variables, or a system of tokens and a README), shown beside the plugin's directions on the sheet and never written to a ledger; a value of it against one the owner settled is a question, and the ledger wins until the owner answers.

A file written from the design ledgers for a tool that does not read them, a DESIGN.md or a design system bundle, stamped with the state of the ledgers it was written from; the gate is red when a ledger changes and the export is not written again, and an export is never read back as a ledger.

The owner's word that the design system bundle of one repository may go to one tool from outside, written as a row of the decision ledger with their name and day, and taken back the same way; nothing is sent without it.
terms.source: The specification of outside plugs, 2026-11-23, open question 7

terms.meaning: To make an item of an outside source fit the repository before it is taken in: record it as taken down, record every change to its code as a patch with its reason, and every rule it is let off as an exemption. Distinct from conformance, which is the state of matching what the system decided: conform is the work that brings an outside item to it.
terms.source: The specification of choose before make, conform before intake, 2026-11-24

terms.meaning: A change to the code of an outside item, kept in its conform record with its reason and its diff, applied in order on the item as taken down. The only way the item's code is changed: a hand edit is not a patch.
terms.source: Common practice: patches kept on upstream code

terms.meaning: A rule an outside item is let off, kept in its conform record with the rule, the file it is let off in (or the configuration file that lets its folder off) and a person's reason.
terms.source: The specification of choose before make, conform before intake, 2026-11-24

terms.meaning: The products one person or team makes that share a core: the same answers to the shared design questions, and blocks proved in more than one of them.
terms.source: The owner's note on a meta layer for many repositories, 2026-11-13

terms.meaning: The core design system of a product family, as a folder of a fixed, versioned shape outside every repository of the family: its declaration, the answers it shares, its graduated blocks and its members' reports.
terms.source: The specification of the family core born through the plugin, 2026-11-25

terms.meaning: An answer of the family core every repository of the family keeps as it is and is not asked again; a member that differs asks the family's owner or keeps an exception with a reason.
terms.source: The specification of the family core born through the plugin, 2026-11-25

terms.meaning: An answer of the family core a new repository of the family starts from and may change, with the change and its reason recorded.
terms.source: The specification of the family core born through the plugin, 2026-11-25

terms.meaning: The four questions a person answers before a family core is built: the family's name, the answers locked, the answers left as defaults, and where the core lives.
terms.source: The specification of the family core born through the plugin, 2026-11-25
